newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Shell still sees major African oil and gas finds.
newsitem.headline: Shell still sees major African oil and gas finds.

text.p: Significant oil and gas reserves are still to be found in Africa, Shell International exploration and production vice president Erik van Scherpenzeel said on Friday.

Shell's own in-house estimates indicated that about 50 billion barrels of oil and 350 trillion cubic feet (tcf) of gas could still be discovered in Africa, increasing the continent's share of total world oil reserves from seven percent to 13 percent.
Its share of gas reserves could rise from seven to 10 percent.
"These are significant figures," van Scherpenzeel told the Africa Upstream conference.

He outlined Shell's activities in Africa and was particularly upbeat about the growth potential of Angola, Congo and Ivory Coast. He said they were set to become "significant forces" in the African energy world.

But he warned that if African countries wanted to attract investment in oil and gas production, they would have to be able to offer political stability and sound legislative regimes for the oil and gas industries.
Van Scherpenzeel welcomed the "new realism" and more acceptable terms and conditions being offered by some countries.
But he hoped that greater flexibility could be offered, especially when oil companies embarked on more expensive deep water exploration.
